                  </ns0:note> I will overturn <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">As this triplication of the threat speaks the certainty of the event, so the gradual, successive troubles, and overthrows, that this Kingdom should ever after be afflicted with.</ns0:note>, overturn, overturn it, and it shall be no <ns0:hi>more,</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Never re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cover its former glory, and strength, but consume, till the Scepter be quite taken away from <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and way be made for the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> who is he that is to come, whose is the Dominion and to whom the Father will give it, so the final desolation of the temporal Kingdom of the seed of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> which was most heavy tidings to the carnal Jew is threatned, and the eternal Kingdom of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> most joyful tidings to the believing Jews, is promised.</ns0:note> until he come, whose right it is, and I will give it <ns0:hi>him.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 ¶ And thou, son of man, <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">In ver. 19. and 20. you had the mention of <ns0:hi>Rabbath</ns0:hi> chief City of the <ns0:hi>Ammonites</ns0:hi> in equal danger with <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> but while <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> is threatned, <ns0:hi>Rabbath</ns0:hi> is no farther minded, till now God directs the Prophet to declare the ruine thereof.</ns0:note> prophesie, and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Zeph. 2.9.</ns0:note> concerning the <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">A stout, but proud, injurious, and insulting people.</ns0:note> Ammonites, and concerning their reproach <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />with they reproacht <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> in the day of <ns0:hi>Israels</ns0:hi> afflictions as <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 49.1. and chap. 25.3, 5, 6. and blasphemed the God of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>; even say thou, the sword, <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">All warlike preparations are made against you.</ns0:note> The sword <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> drawn <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The War is declared, and your enemy hath drawn the Sword, <ns0:hi>vid.</ns0:hi> 9, 10, 11.</ns0:note>, for the slaughter <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">To make waste, by avenging former quarrels, and affronts the <ns0:hi>Babylonish</ns0:hi> King comes out with bloody mind a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst you O <ns0:hi>Ammonites</ns0:hi>! you countenanced <ns0:hi>Ismael,</ns0:hi> who slew <ns0:hi>Gedaliah</ns0:hi> Viceroy by <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzars</ns0:hi> appointment, and you would have set <ns0:hi>Ismael</ns0:hi> on the Throne, this affront you shall satis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fie for with your blood.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> furbished, to consume be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause of the glittering <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Verse 9, 10.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">War, and desolation indeed hasten on thee, though in mean while thy Astrologers, and Soothsayers promise peace, and prosperity, and deceive thee with fair, but false divinati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, of which <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> warns them, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 27.9.</ns0:note> Whiles they <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 22.28.</ns0:note> see vanity unto thee, whiles they divine a lie unto thee, to bring <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">To bring thee under the Sword of the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans,</ns0:hi> and to destroy thee as the Jews are, who already are fallen under the destroying Sword, to make thee stumble and fall on their necks, as men, that fall among a multitude of slain.</ns0:note> thee upon the necks of <ns0:hi>them that are</ns0:hi> slain, of <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> both Jews, and their King, as <ns0:hi>ver,</ns0:hi> 25. <ns0:hi>let. b.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> the wick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed whose day is come, when their iniquity <ns0:hi>shall have</ns0:hi> an end <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">

                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Some read it without interrogation, as an advice to the <ns0:hi>Ammonites</ns0:hi> to put up the Sword they had drawn for their de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fence, as being to no purpose to resist, if it be an interrogation, 'tis such as more vehemently denieth.                <ns0:p n="31">31 And I will pour out <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">As a flood sweeps all away, so God will let out his indig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nation to overwhelm the <ns0:hi>Ammonites.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> mine indignation up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on thee, I will blow <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">As those who melt down mettals blow upon the Mettal in the Fire, that the Fire might burn the fiercer, and consume the dross.</ns0:note> against thee in the fire of my wrath, and deliver <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Or, as there is no hope to one delivered up to barbarous, merciless ruffians, whose Trade is to destroy, so will God deal with these <ns0:hi>Am<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monites.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> thee into the hand of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>burning.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> brutish men, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> skilful to destroy.</ns0:p>

                     <ns0:hi>Rabbath,</ns0:hi> and thy people.</ns0:note> shalt be for fewel <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Which is soon, and unavoid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ably consumed in such a furnace.</ns0:note> to the fire, thy blood shall be in the midst of the land, thou shalt be no <ns0:hi>more</ns0:hi> remembred <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Thy name shall perish.</ns0:note>: for I the LORD have spoken it.<ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Thou shalt no where be safe, or thy bloud shall not be covered, nor thou buried.</ns0:note>
